signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Hawkish Re-pricing
signals.text: The G10 currency strength scorecard flags a severe divergence as JPY leads all majors with a 1W average gain of +0.872% across 7 pairs, while SEK drops to the bottom at −0.556% across 2 pairs, generating a 1.428% bilateral spread. BoJ hawks are actively stepping up calls for rate hikes, driving Japanese 10Y JGB yields to 2.91% and pushing JPY ESI to +21.0, while Riksbank rate expectations face headwinds from persistent Swedish data misses (SEK ESI −26.7). USD/JPY has dropped to 154.32, breaching below its SMA20/50/200 technical cluster at 158.96/160.48/158.45. Options pricing reflects significant downside demand with USD/JPY 25d RR at −2.55, even as a 275bp Fed-BoJ rate differential favors USD carry. Trade bias: Bullish JPY vs SEK and USD; hawkish BoJ repricing and positive data surprise momentum drive the outperformance. Catalyst: Japan Q2 GDP release at 23:50 UTC — forecast 0.4% QoQ. Risk: A downside surprise in Japanese GDP compresses the yield divergence and halts JPY momentum.

signals.title: AUD/USD — COT + Retail Divergence + RBA Rate Hike Bets
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7222, holding well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7135/0.7041/0.6988 as RBA rate hike bets intensify. CFTC COT data shows Leveraged Funds net long AUD at +50,250 contracts (pctl 94, z +1.79), representing a crowded institutional long position at the upper decile of its 52-week range. Conversely, Myfxbook retail sentiment displays an extreme 90% short exposure, establishing a clear institutional vs. retail positioning divergence. RBA at 4.35% vs. Fed at 3.75% provides a -60bp rate differential (-69bp via AONIA-SOFR OIS) that structurally supports the AUD carry, supported by a positive Australian ESI of +16.3. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; institutional longs and carry support favor trend continuation against retail fading. Catalyst: RBA policy meeting on 29 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: Broad risk aversion compresses commodity currencies and forces a unwind of crowded spec longs.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Options Skew + Policy Hold Alignment
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3545, positioned above its SMA50/200 cluster at 1.3456/1.3447 but remaining below the SMA20 at 1.3555. BPVIX 1M implied volatility runs at 11.0% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, generating a substantial +6.3% Vol Risk Premium that indicates elevated market demand for downside tail protection. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds holding a crowded net long of +47,504 contracts (pctl 93, z +1.27), while 25d Risk Reversals sit at −0.45, reflecting cautious options hedging despite the bullish spot posture. BoE policy rate at 3.75% aligns with SOFR 3.66% vs SONIA 3.73% (-7bp OIS differential favoring GBP), but negative UK data momentum (ESI −9.1) suggests macro headwinds are capping near-term upside. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; elevated vol premium signals market caution ahead of upcoming growth data. Catalyst: UK GDP growth pace release and UK BRC Retail Sales at 23:01 UTC. Risk: A hawkish BoE tone at the 17 Sep meeting forces short covering and drives spot above 1.3600.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Carry Drag vs ECB Rate Hike Expectations
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1632, holding above its SMA20 and SMA50 levels at 1.1611 and 1.1512 while testing resistance below the SMA200 at 1.1638. Fed policy rate at 3.75% vs ECB at 2.40% generates a +135bp yield advantage for the USD (+147bp via SOFR-€STR OIS), imposing a structural drag on EUR upside despite market expectations for ECB tightening. Eurozone growth showed resilience with Q2 GDP YoY print at 1.2% (vs 1.0% forecast), lifting EUR ESI to +5.4. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short EUR at −52,784 contracts (pctl 31), though WoW flows added +2,527 contracts. Options volatility shows IV at 7.1% vs HV30 at 4.7% (VRP +2.4%), indicating elevated options hedging demand, while 25d RR sits at a neutral −0.19. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; positive Eurozone economic surprises compete with persistent USD carry advantage. Catalyst: ECB monetary policy decision on 10 Sep. Risk: A dovish ECB guidance shift reinforces the rate differential drag toward 1.1500.
